coef_method: PER-TIDE coefficient: C = a + b*R + c*cosD + d*sinD + e*cos2D + f*sin2D + g*cosA + h*sinA, where R = per-tide equilibrium semidiurnal range (M2,S2,N2,K2 Doodson + Schureman nodal), D = 2*(s-h) spring/neap angle, A = s-p perigee angle. The official coefficient is per-high-tide and regional (Brest==Yeu, verified identical). Fitted to all 705 official 2026 per-tide coefficients (services.data.shom.fr .../spm/coeff) under the same phase-paired convention the app displays (each actual high tide gets the nearest equilibrium high, local phase lag ~3.35h): stdev ~3.8 points, no monthly bias, purely astronomical so multi-year stable.
fit_method: least-squares of Z0 + 27 constituents on the CONTINUOUS 5-min SHOM water-level curves for Jul 20 - Oct 27 2026 (8 overlapping 11-day windows, 28800 pts, services.data.shom.fr .../spm/wl, tools/wl_*.json). The 100-day baseline resolves the near-degenerate semidiurnal beats (M2-S2 14.8d, M2-N2 27.5d, M2-K2 29.6d) that a short window cannot: the previous 17-day fit traded their amplitudes off against each other and drifted anti-phased within ~2 months. Nodal correction (Schureman) per-observation, exact astronomical periods. Validated vs the official SHOM high/low tables (maree.info, independent of the curve): Aug 27-Sep 3 times mean 5min/heights 3cm, Oct 22-28 times 5min/heights 2cm; extrapolation +25..31d gives 6min/7cm. Multi-year sane to 2040.
